body: So we can add a safeguard for this, for sure. But keep in mind that having `@Valid` on `Object` will cause issues. We need to gather the types that will be validated by Hibernate Validator, it cannot be random ones.
Yeah, quarkus needs a list of all types. but a safeguard might help in case someone else has this problem.

issue.title: Don't consider the hierarchy of Object when marked with @Valid
Hibernate-validator: @Valid annotation on the Object type attribute.
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
If `@Valid` annotation is added to the `Object` type attribute the `HibernateValidatorProcessor` will add all sub-classes of the Object to the list `classesToBeValidated` for the `HibernateValidatorRecorder`
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/ebfeffcebfdbbf5ab7fc8c873eeecde90f8bdee2/extensions/hibernate-validator/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/validator/deployment/HibernateValidatorProcessor.java#L251

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/ebfeffcebfdbbf5ab7fc8c873eeecde90f8bdee2/extensions/hibernate-validator/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/validator/deployment/HibernateValidatorProcessor.java#L310

For example if we use the flyway for the database migration the HibernateValidatorProcessor will add all the flyway optional runtime classes. For example: 'org.flywaydb.core.internal.scanner.classpath.jboss.JBossVFSv3ClassPathLocationScanner'

**To Reproduce**
Example rest controller
```
@Path("/test")
public class TestRestController {

    @GET
    public DataDTO post() {
        return new DataDTO();
    }

    @Data
    public static class DataDTO {
        private @Valid Object name;
    }
}
```
